answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with lottery-gated enrollment: new identities may only join during a short window each epoch, and a public lottery admits a fixed few, like a canyon pass that opens once and lets a single file through. A farm cannot mint ten thousand fakes on demand; each must win a separate draw, so its odds collapse while its costs pile up. One honest agent waits for the next window once, passes through the quartz gate, and stands at the vertex of trust it earned.
